attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No current argument proves that every one-sided local certificate predicate family of total size below N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} misses at least N^{epsilon-o(1)} positive bags on the actual generated range.
steps: Fix epsilon, q in ((1+epsilon)/2,1+epsilon), rho<1+epsilon, and L=(log N)^d with d>1.
Define H_N as the OR of N^q generated 3CNF SAT instances and keep C(G_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} as the shared interface cost.
Assume a (K,E,s)-SLC cover. Build a circuit that computes G_N(x), evaluates every A_i on its indexed formula G_N(x)_{j_i}, and ORs the K one-sided outputs.
Soundness of A_i prevents false positives on H_N^{-1}(0); completeness except E positives leaves only E missed x values.
Patch the E missed positive inputs by hardwired equality tests of size O(EN), giving C(H_N)<=C(G_N)+O(K(s+L^{O(1)})+EN).
Therefore a proposed source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} must imply a superthreshold lower bound against SLC covers, not merely against explicit witnesses or partial terms.
The old target bridge still works: if SAT has size n^c circuits, each length-L query costs L^c=N^{o(1)}, so H_N has size N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid route lemma and falsifier audit, not a proof of P != NP. The missing step is a non-natural, non-leaky SLC cover lower bound for a concrete generator; partial witness entropy and formula-range entropy do not imply it.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: sound local certificate cover gate

assumptions: epsilon>0 is fixed and all o(1) terms are with respect to N.
C(G_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} as a shared multi-output circuit.
Each local predicate is one-sided sound for SAT on all length-L 3CNFs, not merely on the generated range.
Missed positive inputs may be patched nonuniformly by equality gates of size O(EN).
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<=M} SAT(G_N(x)_j), where x in {0,1}^N, M=floor(N^q), G_N emits M length-L 3CNFs, L=(log N)^d with d>1, and the source model is nonuniform fan-in-two Boolean circuits for H_N.
target object: SAT on length L instances, with target consequence SAT notin P/poly obtained only through the separate substitution bridge when max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.

controlled interface: a shared multi-output generator G_N of size N^{rho+o(1)} including output routing N^{q+o(1)}, followed either by SAT circuits or by local one-sided certificate predicates applied to generated formulas.
target-preserving condition: q,rho<1+epsilon, q>(1+epsilon)/2 for dense-tuple blocking, L=(log N)^d with d>1 to avoid lookup collapse, and no nonuniform advice about x except through G_N outputs.

An (K,E,s)-SLC cover is a family {(j_i,A_i)}_{i<=K} where j_i in [M], A_i is a size-s circuit on length-L 3CNF encodings, A_i(phi)=1 implies phi is satisfiable, and all but E inputs x with H_N(x)=1 have some i with A_i(G_N(x)_{j_i})=1.

If H_N has a subthreshold SLC cover with few missed positive inputs, then H_N has subthreshold general circuits, so an N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} source lower bound must first rule out these covers.

assumptions: Generated instances are encoded as 3CNFs, so term verification is deterministic and local in the formula encoding.
The generator outputs can be shared across all term tests.
The cover may miss E positive x values, which are then patched nonuniformly.
definitions: A partial term tau for a 3CNF phi is a partial assignment that hits every clause of phi by setting at least one literal in the clause to true.
A position-indexed term cover is a family {(j_i,tau_i)} whose tests accept x when tau_i hits every clause of G_N(x)_{j_i}.
The test is one-sided sound because a term hitting every clause certifies satisfiability of that emitted 3CNF.

An SLC lower bound proved by a large constructive property of length-L formula truth tables would risk a natural-proofs obstruction. The route must use generator-specific, non-large, or otherwise non-natural structure; it is not automatically outside the barrier.

falsifiers: falsifier: a subthreshold (K,E,N^{o(1)}) SLC cover with K<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} and E<N^{epsilon-o(1)} gives an explicit small circuit for H_N.
Low-width backdoor falsifier: if every positive emitted formula has a satisfying term of width b=alpha log N and q+alpha<1+epsilon, enumerating all such terms collapses the source lower bound.
Compressed-certificate falsifier: a size-poly(L) one-sided predicate can represent many partial terms, so large term count alone is not a valid source certificate.
Lookup-boundary falsifier: if L=O(log N) with q+2^L exponent below 1+epsilon, local truth-table predicates replace genuine SAT hardness.
Generator-bias falsifier: if positives lie in a small easy satisfiable subclass such as Horn, 2-SAT, bounded-width, or bounded-backdoor CNFs, SLC cover size may be subthreshold.
Nonuniform leakage falsifier: predicates A_i may contain advice tailored to the generated range; the source lower bound must defeat this advice rather than only uniform algorithms.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Missing SAT-specific depth-preserving simulation from DTIME(m^k) to AC0_d below the lower-bound threshold.
steps: Model the source as a claimed lower bound L_d(m) for SAT_m against AC0_d size s.
Assume for contradiction that SAT is decidable in time m^k.
A P-time decider yields P-uniform Boolean circuits of polynomial size and polynomial depth, not fixed depth d.
To contradict the AC0_d lower bound one must reduce those circuits to depth d with size B_{k,d}(m)<L_d(m).
No such depth-preserving reduction is known or plausible as a black-box statement; PARITY in P violates any universal version.
The derivation therefore proves only SAT notin AC0_d[s], a restricted-class separation already outside the P-vs-NP target.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The lower bound separates NP from a weak circuit class, while P allows polynomial depth and can contain functions with large fixed-depth complexity. The transfer to P is invalid without the named compiler.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: AC0 Depth-Leakage Gate

assumptions: d is fixed independently of m unless explicitly varied.
The AC0 model is standard De Morgan AC0 with NOT gates at inputs and unbounded fan-in AND/OR gates.
The lower bound is for the same SAT slice that the alleged polynomial-time algorithm decides.
The compiler must be uniform enough that a P algorithm cannot hide depth in advice or preprocessing.
definitions: source object: length-m Boolean slice SAT_m of a standard SAT encoding, together with a lower bound L_d(m) against depth-d unbounded-fan-in De Morgan circuits of size s.
target object: SAT notin DTIME(m^k), hence route-level progress toward NP not subset P only after quantifying over every fixed k.
controlled interface: a uniform depth-preserving compiler Sim_{k,d} mapping any m^k-time SAT decider to depth-d AC0 circuits of size B_{k,d}(m) on the identical length-m encoding.
target-preserving condition: L_d(m)>B_{k,d}(m) for all sufficiently large m, with no nonuniform advice leakage, promise change, padding change, or replacement of SAT by an easier restricted language.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The argument refutes only restriction-only or sampled-label certificates. A genuinely global proof invariant, arithmetized lower-bound certificate, or non-natural proof system is outside this falsifier and remains open.
steps: Start with a low-image carrier family R_m={T_1,...,T_M}, M<=2^{Dm+o(m)}, and try to certify one hard row by an O(m)-bit seed selecting t sampled inputs H={x_1,...,x_t}.
Let the certificate provide or derive the labels b_j=T_i(x_j), and let the verifier attempt to use the assertion that no size-s_m circuit matches all pairs (x_j,b_j).

For any H and labels b, build an interpolating DNF: for each positive labeled point add its m-literal minterm, and set arbitrary values off H. This has size O(tm), with a similar bound for all label patterns.
If t<s_m/(A m), the interpolating circuit has size below s_m, so the sampled constraints are compatible with a small circuit regardless of the true row complexity.

For s_m=2^{epsilon m}, any restriction-only certificate must therefore expose Omega(2^{epsilon m}/m) labeled positions, far beyond O(m) certificate length and not compatible with the intended sparse source interface.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-level negative theorem for one source model. It neither constructs a valid MCSP carrier nor proves P != NP; it narrows the admissible source to global, non-restriction proof objects.

assumptions: Unrestricted Boolean circuits over m inputs are the target lower-bound model.
The certificate is restriction-only: all row-dependent semantic information is a set of labeled examples.
epsilon>0 is constant and s_m=2^{epsilon m}.
The carrier may have low distinct-image entropy D, but the falsifier acts before multiplexing.
definitions: source object: a restriction-only direct MCSP row certificate, consisting of a canonical row T_m and t(m) labeled positions (x_j,T_m(x_j)), with no global lower-bound invariant beyond those labels.
target object: a no-side MCSP claim MCSP_m(T_m)>s_m for unrestricted Boolean circuits of size s_m=2^{epsilon m}.
controlled interface: the verifier may use the listed labels and E-uniform row emission, but its soundness argument reduces to the nonexistence of a small circuit consistent with those labels.
target-preserving condition: the source remains O(m)-described, E-time checkable, advice-free, and intended to feed the existing low-D carrier transfer with delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).

candidate_lemmas.statement: Restriction-only direct MCSP row certificates cannot be a valid source for the low-D carrier at constant threshold. If a certificate for a row T:{0,1}^m->{0,1} uses only t labeled positions of T as its semantic evidence, then for t << 2^{epsilon m}/m those labels are consistent with some unrestricted circuit of size at most 2^{epsilon m}. Thus such a certificate cannot soundly prove MCSP(T)>2^{epsilon m}.

assumptions: Proof soundness is for unrestricted nonuniform circuits, not merely uniform algorithms or restricted circuit classes.

No ranked random access circuit below the target MCSP threshold is supplied by the source.
definitions: Proof system P_m is deterministic, advice-free, and verifies a statement about unrestricted circuit size of the emitted row.
The canonical image family has at most 2^{Dm+o(m)} distinct rows and supports E-time distinct-image unranking.
A hard row may be existential inside the image; multiplexing over image rank removes the need for a nonuniform selector.

Restriction-audited aggregate proofs are those whose row-hardness evidence consists only of sampled row labels.

gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: A canonical low-image MCSP carrier with M=2^{Dm} rows; a proposed O(m)-bit certificate picks sampled positions in one row and claims these samples rule out all circuits of size s=2^{epsilon m}.

gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: sample exponent theta in t=2^{theta m}/m, ranging from theta=0 for O(m) samples to theta=epsilon at the interpolation threshold.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 40 adds a concrete source-side no-go theorem: subthreshold point evidence cannot certify a direct hard MCSP row, because arbitrary labels on t positions have unrestricted circuits of size O(tm).
